scams.name: Perth Airport Taxi & Uber 'Fake Surge' Overcharge
scams.tldr: You land at Perth Airport at 6am and try to book an Uber to your hotel in Northbridge. The app quotes $125 — flagged as 3.5× surge — for a trip Google Maps says should be $35. You wait, it creeps higher. You finally switch to a taxi at the rank, which 'agrees' to a flat $90 cash fare. The actual metered fare would be $52.
scams.description:
r/perth threads describe the same play running on repeat. Drivers complain that Uber pricing balloons in the predawn hours because nobody accepts the early rides — the surge climbs, somebody finally takes it, and the next FIFO worker pays $90 for a $35 trip. The taxi-rank variant is older and cruder: a driver waves you over, says the meter is "slow tonight," and offers a flat $90 cash to Northbridge. The actual metered fare with the $5 airport surcharge is around $52. The 4am–6am and 5pm–7pm windows are when fly-in-fly-out mining traffic genuinely thins out the rideshare pool, and the drivers who stay on coordinate informally to keep prices high.

Your fix in 2026 is simpler than ever. Perth Airport's rail link opened in late 2022 and connects T3/T4 to Redcliffe and onward to the CBD for under $5 — tourist-proof and timetable-locked. Uber and DiDi both have designated pickup bays at all terminals; if one app is surging, check the other before you commit. Wait 10 minutes if the price is silly — surges almost always reset once drivers see riders walking away. The standard rideshare fare from PER to Perth CBD is $35–$55 off-peak, and a metered taxi is roughly the same plus the $5 airport surcharge. Anything over $80 means walk back to the rank, find the train, and let this driver chase the next jet-lagged tourist.
scams.avoidance: Take the Perth Airport train to CBD (<$5, every 15 min) as the tourist-proof option. Use Uber or DiDi from the rideshare bay — typical CBD fare is $35–$55. Compare Uber, DiDi and Bolt before ordering — one is usually normally priced. Wait 10 minutes and retry if surges are extreme — they reset. Insist on meter and card tap for any taxi — screenshot the receipt.
scams.location: Perth Airport T1 international, T3/T4 domestic taxi ranks and rideshare bays

scams.name: Perth Facebook / Gumtree Fake Rental Scam
scams.tldr: You find a Fremantle share-room listed on Facebook Marketplace for $200/week — great photos, a friendly 'landlord' who says he's currently in Melbourne and needs a bank-transfer deposit of $400 to hold the room. You send it. When you arrive in Fremantle, the address is a family home, and the Facebook account has vanished.
scams.description:
r/perth and r/AusTravel threads document this one running constantly, with new arrivals posting variations of the same story every few weeks: a Facebook Marketplace room in Fremantle or Subiaco, photos that look great, a landlord who claims to be in Melbourne or Singapore for work, and a polite request to lock the room in with a $400–$800 transfer. Locals in the threads say the same thing every time — Facebook listings for Perth rentals are now so scam-saturated that most long-term renters refuse to use the platform at all. The scammers lift photos from real estate sites, spin up a clean-looking profile, and target backpackers and Working Holiday Visa arrivals who don't yet have an Australian bank to dispute the transfer through.

Your defense is absolute: no in-person viewing, no deposit. For short stays, book only via airbnb.com or booking.com through the official app — never through a Facebook DM or Gumtree listing. For sharehouses, inspect the property and meet current housemates before paying anything. Perth-specific: legitimate listings cluster on flatmates.com.au and the University of Western Australia's accommodation board; Facebook Marketplace has the worst fake-to-legit ratio of any channel. If a landlord refuses to let you walk through the door before the deposit hits their account, the door doesn't exist — report the listing to ScamWatch at scamwatch.gov.au and WA Police on 131 444.
scams.avoidance: Never pay any deposit before an in-person viewing and key handover. Use airbnb.com / booking.com only for short stays, via the app or a bookmarked URL. For sharehouses use flatmates.com.au and inspect in person before paying. Reverse image-search photos in Google Images before any financial commitment. Report scams to ScamWatch at scamwatch.gov.au and WA Police on 131 444.
scams.location: Perth CBD, Fremantle, Subiaco, Northbridge — sharehouse + short-stay market

scams.name: Rottnest Island Ferry & 'Day Tour' Upsell
scams.tldr: You Google 'Rottnest Island day trip' and an aggressive booking site offers 'ferry + bike + lunch' for $139 — 'the cheapest way to visit Rottnest.' You pay. On the day you arrive at Fremantle and learn the ferry portion is with an operator that runs only on odd-numbered weekdays, the bike is a basic unit without helmet, and the 'lunch' is a voucher for a Hotel Rottnest meal that's not actually included.
scams.description:
Rottnest isn't a traditional scam — it's a genuinely expensive day trip ($50+ admission fee, $50–$90 ferry, $30+ bike hire) and r/perth regulars will be the first to admit the island has been priced for capacity, not for backpackers, for years. The trap is the third-party booking site that wraps a cheap ferry around vague "inclusions" and then under-delivers each one: the ferry runs only certain weekdays and doesn't match your dates, the bike is a single-speed clunker without a helmet, and the lunch voucher is good for exactly one dish at one Hotel Rottnest counter with a 90-minute queue at peak. By the time you've spent the morning sorting it out, you've burned half the daylight.

Your defense is to book directly with the two established ferry operators: Rottnest Express (rottnestexpress.com.au, Fremantle and Perth CBD departures) and Sealink Rottnest Island (sealinkrottnest.com.au, Hillarys Boat Harbour and Fremantle). Buy the Rottnest Island Authority admission fee separately at rottnestisland.com to avoid bundled markups. Rent bikes on-island at Pedal & Flipper (the official monopoly at the main settlement) or bring your own — either way, bike rental with helmet is $30 per day. Pay everything by credit card so you have chargeback leverage if the third-party operator no-shows on a single "inclusion."
scams.avoidance: Book directly with Rottnest Express (rottnestexpress.com.au) or Sealink (sealinkrottnest.com.au). Buy the Rottnest Island Authority admission separately at rottnestisland.com. Rent bikes on-island at Pedal & Flipper — $30/day with helmet. Pay by credit card for chargeback protection. Read TripAdvisor reviews of the exact ferry operator from the last 6 months.
scams.location: Hillarys Boat Harbour, Fremantle B Shed terminal, Perth CBD Barrack Street jetty

scams.name: Fremantle Markets & 'Cappuccino Strip' Overcharge
scams.tldr: You wander into Fremantle Markets on a Saturday and pick out a pile of touristy pieces — a wooden boomerang, a few didgeridoos, a t-shirt. At the register the total is $245. You paid by tap and didn't check the itemization. Only later do you notice the 'wooden boomerang' was charged at $89 — an authentic Indigenous-artist piece — when you bought a $25 mass-produced souvenir.
scams.description:
r/perth threads on Fremantle have a recurring complaint: the Cappuccino Strip is a row of overpriced pubs and tobacco-shop fronts, and the markets themselves run on flexible pricing that quietly punishes anyone who pays without checking. The pattern is mundane and effective. Stall operators ring up the souvenir boomerang at the same price as a certified Indigenous-artist piece, multi-item purchases get compressed into one tap-total nobody queries, and outdoor seating on the strip carries a surcharge that's only printed on the inside menu. Authentic Indigenous art is genuinely expensive — a real Pinaroo boomerang sits at $150+ — and a real arts center will hand you provenance paperwork without being asked. The overcharge scam lives entirely in the price gap between mass-produced and authentic.

Your defense: pay by card and always request an itemized receipt before you walk away. Don't buy Indigenous art at generic market stalls if the operator can't provide Aboriginal Art Association certification — the Fremantle Arts Center and the Japingka Gallery are the legitimate sources with artist provenance. On the Cappuccino Strip, menu prices are often posted inside only; ask before sitting down whether the outdoor seat carries a surcharge (it usually does). Tap for every purchase, count the line items on the receipt against what's in your bag, and challenge any total that doesn't add up before you leave the stall.
scams.avoidance: Always request itemized receipts — count the items on the receipt match what you bought. Buy Indigenous art only from certified galleries (Japingka, Fremantle Arts Center). Check menu prices before sitting outside at Cappuccino Strip cafes. Pay by card tap and screenshot receipts immediately. Challenge rounded totals politely — most operators correct errors when asked.
scams.location: Fremantle Markets (South Tce), Cappuccino Strip (South Tce between Collie & High)

scams.name: Perth Backpacker Hostel Prepay Scam
scams.tldr: You land in Perth on a Working Holiday Visa and a Facebook backpacker group has a 'manager' offering a Northbridge hostel bed at $180/week — pay four weeks upfront by bank transfer and get the first week free. You send $540 (3 weeks). The 'manager' stops responding; the hostel, when you turn up, has never heard of them.
scams.description:
r/perth and r/AusTravel both have backpacker-scam threads with the same beats: a Working Holiday Visa arrival pays one or two weeks up front by bank transfer, the "manager" goes silent, and the actual hostel reception has never heard the name. Locals in the threads warn that even long-term Perth residents fall for variants of this — it's not a tourist-only mistake. The scammers know exactly who they're targeting: WHV arrivals who don't yet have an Australian bank account to dispute the transfer through, who are jet-lagged from a Southeast Asia stopover, and who are unlikely to pursue $540 through small-claims court before their next regional move.

Your rule: never pay a hostel before check-in. Verified Perth backpacker hostels (The Old Swan Barracks, Billabong Backpackers, Emperors Crown, Zebra Inn, One World Backpackers) take payment at reception or via HostelWorld and Booking.com — both have platform protection if the bed doesn't exist. For sharehouses, insist on in-person viewing and meet current flatmates. Pay rent only after you have the key in your hand. The Perth WHV community uses the Perth Working Holiday Facebook group and r/perth itself as a crowd-sourced reality check — post the listing before you transfer anything. If a "manager" insists on a bank transfer before you can walk through the door, that hostel doesn't exist — keep your money and book a real bed on HostelWorld for the night.
scams.avoidance: Book hostels only via HostelWorld, Booking.com, or directly at reception. Never pay more than one night's stay before check-in — not even a deposit. Cross-check any Facebook post in the Perth Working Holiday group before paying. Keep a copy of your bank-transfer reference number — needed for WA Police reports. If scammed, file a police report at police.wa.gov.au and ScamWatch.
scams.location: Perth CBD and Northbridge hostel market, Facebook/Gumtree WHV groups

scams.name: Northbridge Nightlife Tab Inflation & Card Skim
scams.tldr: You hand your card to the bartender at a busy Northbridge club to open a tab. At 2am the bill is $380 for a group of four — triple what you actually drank. The card reader 'tapped twice accidentally' on one transaction, there's a $25 'service charge' you weren't told about, and security is visibly close when you review the bill.
scams.description:
r/perth threads on Northbridge are a long catalogue of patience-tested late nights: this is where WA's nightclub licensing is deliberately concentrated, so the same tab-inflation playbook running in Fortitude Valley and Cavill Avenue runs here too. The specifically Perth variants are mechanical: card readers that "system error" and ring up the same round twice, tab items for drinks nobody ordered showing up at 2am, and undisclosed event-night cover charges quietly rolled into the final bill while security hovers a step behind you.

Your defense is identical to any Australian nightlife district. Never open a tab; pay round-by-round with card tap. Keep your card in your wallet and only tap personally — never hand it over. Scrutinize every receipt before signing. If a tab is unavoidable for a group purchase, appoint one trusted person to hold it and photograph each drink receipt as it comes back. If the bill is wrong, ask for the venue manager, photograph the itemized total, and dispute the charge with your bank the next business day — Australian card networks side with the cardholder when the venue can't produce signed receipts for every line item.
scams.avoidance: Never open a tab — pay round-by-round with card tap. Keep your card in your wallet; tap personally, never hand over. Photograph every bar receipt so totals are verifiable at the end of the night. Challenge bills calmly — request the venue manager and itemization. Chargeback disputed charges next business day with your bank.
scams.location: Northbridge — William Street, James Street, Lake Street nightlife strip
